source:
Imagine a fashion game called Runway Royale. It has the fun of creating outfits and competing in fashion shows, but with much more to do between rounds.
🌟 Main Lobby
As players join, they enter a huge luxury fashion mall with glowing waterfalls, glass elevators, giant digital billboards, music, and a spinning central runway. Around the lobby are portals to different game modes, a daily reward fountain, trading plaza, photo studio, and event stage.
👗 Dressing Booths
Instead of everyone changing in the open, every player gets their own private dressing booth.
Full-length smart mirrors
Outfit save slots
Makeup and hair stations
Skin tone and body customization
Accessory organizers
Outfit randomizer
Favorite clothing section
Booth themes you can unlock (Fairy, Modern, Princess, Cyber, Beach, Cottagecore, etc.)
🛍️ Non-VIP Fashion Area
Everyone can use hundreds of beautiful items including:
Dresses
Jeans
Skirts
Jackets
Hoodies
Sneakers
Heels
Boots
Hats
Glasses
Hairstyles
Makeup
Jewelry
Bags
Nails
Face accessories
New free clothes are added every week so non-VIP players never feel left behind.
💎 VIP Fashion Lounge
VIP players enter through sparkling golden doors into a luxury boutique.
VIP includes:
Exclusive designer collections
Animated dresses
Wings
Luxury gowns
Fantasy outfits
Premium hairstyles
Designer handbags
Exclusive makeup
Particle effects
Glowing accessories
Special poses
VIP-only dressing booths
Private runway practice room
VIP chat lounge
🎭 Fashion Themes
Every round gives a random theme, such as:
Mermaid Royalty
First Day of School
Pop Star
Vampire Queen
Winter Wonderland
Space Explorer
Cottage Princess
Y2K
Gothic Glam
Red Carpet
Fairy Forest
Pirate Captain
Summer Vacation
Magical Academy
Celebrity Look
Players have 5 minutes to create their outfits.
✨ Runway Show
When time is up:
Players walk down a stunning animated runway.
Spotlights follow each model.
Cameras flash.
Music changes with each round.
Players strike poses before reaching the judges.
⭐ Voting
Instead of simple stars, players earn points for:
Creativity
Theme accuracy
Styling
Color coordination
Overall wow factor
The top three receive crowns, confetti, and bonus rewards.
🏆 Progression
Players level up through fashion ranks:
Fashion Rookie
Trendsetter
Style Icon
Elite Designer
Supermodel
Fashion Legend
Runway Royalty
Higher ranks unlock badges, titles, booth decorations, and special victory animations.
📸 Extra Features
Outfit photo studio
Trading accessories
Fashion clubs with friends
Weekly tournaments
Seasonal battle pass
Daily styling challenges
Pet companions
Color wheel with millions of shades
Fabric textures (silk, denim, velvet, lace, leather)
Weather effects on runways
Fashion magazine where winning outfits are displayed
🌈 Why it stands out
Instead of only dressing up and voting, players can collect rare clothing, decorate their own dressing booth, climb fashion leagues, complete quests, trade cosmetics, join fashion teams, and explore a beautiful world that keeps growing with new updates. It feels like a fashion-themed adventure rather than just a runway game, making it deeper and more rewarding while staying fun for casual players.

answers.ask: Is the mall lobby, the runway and the VIP wing all one continuous space, or does each mode sit on its own map reached through the portals?
answers.answer: Keep the luxury mall lobby and VIP wing as one continuous shared space, with portals leading to separate runway-show maps for rounds.

answers.ask: Are the dressing booths private per-player instances, or physical rooms in the shared lobby that anyone can walk into?
answers.answer: Dressing booths are private per-player instances, so each player can customize outfits without others entering or seeing their booth.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: Is the mall lobby, the runway and the VIP wing all one continuous space, or does each mode sit on its own map reached through the portals? A: Keep the luxury mall lobby and VIP wing as one continuous shared space, with portals leading to separate runway-show maps for rounds.
- [author] shape — Q: Are the dressing booths private per-player instances, or physical rooms in the shared lobby that anyone can walk into? A: Dressing booths are private per-player instances, so each player can customize outfits without others entering or seeing their booth.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a large luxury fashion-mall hub with glowing waterfalls, glass elevators, giant digital billboards, a spinning central display runway, and portals arranged around the lobby. Connect the hub directly to a non-VIP fashion area with displays for clothing, shoes, hats, glasses, hair, makeup, jewelry, bags, nails, and face accessories; a trading plaza; daily-reward fountain; outfit photo studio; event stage; and a fashion-magazine display. Sparkling gold doors open into a continuous VIP wing containing a luxury boutique, exclusive dressing access, private runway-practice room, and VIP lounge.

The portals lead to separate runway-show maps with an animated catwalk, pose point, judges' end, spotlights, and camera-flash staging, dressed for rotating fashion themes. Private per-player dressing-booth instances contain full-length smart mirrors, makeup and hair stations, body and skin customization, accessory organizers, saved and favorite outfit displays, and selectable booth themes.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Roleplay & Avatar Sim, specifically dress-up and fashion-show play.

## Shape and preset
Use `hub-portals`, outside the genre's usual set, because one mall hub sends players to separate runway maps and private booth instances. The matched preset is Dress Up, substituting this multi-map hub container while retaining its social and photo-oriented features.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` for the central mall and trading plaza; `vignette-photo` for the outfit studio; `water-body` for the glowing waterfalls and reward fountain; `landmark-focal` for the spinning central runway and billboards; `teleporter-link` for visible mode portals and booth access; `trigger-task`, taken from Simulation, for the daily-reward fountain; and `zone-graphics`, taken from Entertainment, for contained high-detail waterfall, glass, billboard, and runway-effect clusters.

## Layout requirements
Place `teleporter-link` endpoints around the mall, paired to each separate runway map and private booth instance. Place one `trigger-task` at the reward fountain. Keep private booth destinations isolated per player.

## Layout components
Segments are Main Mall and VIP Wing as connected zones on one shared map; Dressing Booth as a private instanced `map` using `interior-single`; and Runway Show as separate themed `map` instances using `stage-runway`. Mall circulation links every venue without entering the portals accidentally.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: luxury composition leads for each segment, while the portal endpoints preserve the authored map relationships.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large for the mall, with small booth and medium runway submaps preserving fine detail. The theme is luminous luxury fashion with colorful themed shows. Use `P4` for separate runway and booth maps and `CHECK` for the flowing-water features.

notes: Dropped implicit submap shapes `interior-single` and `stage-runway` because this schema accepts exactly one `shape`, and only `hub-portals` was specified as the scene shape.

No explicit layout composition/terrain/boundary/paths siting strings were provided beyond the portal-circulation guidance, so `layout.composition`, `layout.terrain`, `layout.boundary`, and `layout.paths` are left empty/empty-array.
Option texts were translated into English per instruction; the blob was already in English.
The schema provided does not define `render.then`; included as `then` would violate schema, so it was not emitted.
